title: Retroactive amnesty window and telemetry-driven soft-cap adjustments for tenant rate limits
creator: Ava Patel
description: Problem: Several reserved-capacity customers experienced unexpected hard throttles immediately after monthly quota resets and during short-term burst transfers. Root causes included late-arriving usage events, clock skew between ingestion pipelines, and conservative hard-cap enforcement for newly provisioned microcredits. Proposal: introduce a short retroactive 'amnesty window' at quota reset boundaries and an automated telemetry-driven soft-cap stage that temporarily relaxes enforcement while reconciliation completes. The feature should be safe for billing integrity, observable, and reversible.
acceptance_criteria: Introduce a configurable amnesty window (default 10 minutes) after daily/monthly quota resets where hard throttles are suppressed and requests are accepted under a soft-cap accounting layer.

Soft-cap must be recorded in the ledger as provisional usage with a reconciled finalization step that either converts provisional usage into billed tokens or triggers a compensating adjustment (credit/invoice correction) if overcount detected.
Telemetry-based triggers automatically shorten or extend the amnesty window per-tenant depending on late-event rate and clock-drift signals (max extension 2 hours), with safe upper bound enforced.
No user-visible double-charging: provisional acceptance must not cause immediate billing; final billing decision must be reflected in invoice and shown in Console billing UI.
Metrics in Console: provisional_accept_rate, reconciled_conversion_rate, late_event_rate, mean_reconciliation_lag. Alerting configured for reconciled_conversion_rate < 95% over 1h for any tenant.
Automated rollback toggles and feature flagging present for canary deployments and emergency disable.
End-to-end tests covering late-event scenarios, timezone-shifted tenants, DST/leap-second edges, and reserved-pool cross-transfer flows.
implementation_plan: Add amnesty window config to quota controller and tenant entitlement metadata (default values editable per-tenant via Console).
Implement provisional ledger rows (provisional=true) in metering DB for accepted tokens during amnesty; ensure idempotent write paths and tombstoning for duplicates.

Extend reconciler job to finalize provisional rows: validate late events, sum definitive usage, and emit conversion or compensating credit transactions. Reconciler must be able to process backfills and late-arrivals deterministically.
Introduce a soft-cap enforcement mode in rate-limiter: allow requests while tracking provisional consumption and mark requests with an audit header (X-Quota-Provisional: true).
Add telemetry extraction (ClickHouse query) to compute late_event_rate and mean_reconciliation_lag; feed signals into the autoscaler-style amnesty controller to adjust windows.
Add console UI components: tenant-level amnesty settings, provisional usage tab, and reconciled conversion reports.
Create feature flag and rollout plan (per-region, per-tenant canary), and GitHub PRs for runtime, metering service, reconciler, and console changes.
rollout_plan: Phase A - Internal canary: enable for internal QA tenants only (1 day). Monitor reconciled_conversion_rate and error logs.
Phase B - Small-customer canary: enable for 5 low-risk customers (~72 hours). Validate billing exports and invoice previews.
Phase C - Reserved pools pilot: enable for a subset of reserved capacity customers under opt-in. Monitor reserved-pool transfer correctness.
Phase D - Gradual GA: 10% of tenants -> 50% -> 100% over 2 weeks, with kill-switch at each step.
At each phase run a reconciliation audit comparing provisional accepted tokens to final billed tokens and publish a pilot report to Confluence.
monitoring_and_metrics: Dashboards: Provisional vs Final Usage (per-tenant), Late Event Distribution (by source), Amnesty Window Extensions (count).
SLOs: Mean reconciliation lag < 30m for 95% tenants; reconciled_conversion_rate >= 98% in steady state.
Alerts: reconciled_conversion_rate < 95% (P1), mean_reconciliation_lag > 2h (P2), unexpected growth in provisional_accept_rate (P2).
Logging: every provisional acceptance must log tenant, provisional_id, sequence_token, and source_pipeline; reconciler must log decisions and confidence reasons for conversion or crediting.
rollback_plan: Feature flag immediate disable that switches rate-limiter back to hard-cap enforcement and rejects further provisional acceptances.
When flag disabled, reconciler continues to finalize outstanding provisional rows but no new provisional rows are created.

If data corruption or billing divergence detected, run compensating-credit job and notify affected customers and Billing ops. Create incident runbook linking to PRs and Confluence postmortem template.
Keep historical snapshot of ledger before GA (weekly snapshot) to allow ledger-level rollback if necessary.

decisions: Default amnesty window set to 10 minutes based on historical late-event distribution; can be overridden per-tenant.
Provisional usage will be stored in the same ledger table with a provisional flag rather than a separate store to simplify reconciliation and auditing.
Soft-cap acceptance will not increment immediate billing counters exposed to customers; billing preview and invoices are updated only after reconciliation.
Maximum automatic amnesty window extension capped at 2 hours to limit long-term exposure.
Feature gated behind per-tenant flag and global kill-switch for fast rollback during incidents.
